Subject: Novus AI — SLO fitment & validation plan for dedicated pool

Hi Caroline / Raj (copied if useful),

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great discussion on the latency needs for your live summarization product. Quick recap and a proposed validation approach so we can get to a committed Dedicated pool size and HW recommendation.

Call highlights:
- Target SLOs: p95 latency <= 150ms for short streaming summaries (<= 256 tokens), p95 <= 250ms for longer end-to-end flows (with KV cache warmed).
- Throughput expectations: steady-state 3k tokens/sec with spikes to ~8k tokens/sec during 2–3 daily peaks.
- Concurrent sessions: 150–250 active streams concurrently.
- Acceptable fallbacks: if peak latency degrades beyond 200ms we want automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant for non-critical tenants.

Initial HW observations and recommendation (high level):
- H100 (PCIe/HBM variant): best for aggressive KV cache and mixed precision kernels for streaming; expected to give ~20–30% better p95 for the streaming case vs A100 at similar batch sizes.
- A100 80GB: strong choice for cost-per-token on long-context, high-throughput bursts; good for heavier batch workloads where streaming latency is less critical.
- L40S: fine for prototyping and non-streaming heavy throughput but we expect higher p95 for low-latency streaming.

Proposed validation plan (what Redwood will run with your sign-off):
1) Microbenchmarks: per-GPU single-worker p95/p99 across representative prompt shapes (short streaming, long summarization) to measure baseline kernel performance.
2) End-to-end synthetic load: driving token-level traffic that mirrors your 80/20 short/long split; run at 50%, 100%, and 150% of expected peak to validate headroom.
3) KV cache warmup scenario: measure p95 once cache is warmed (simulate 10k unique sessions then re-hit top-100 prefixes).
4) Concurrency sweep: measure p95 while increasing concurrent sessions from 50 up to 300 to find knee points.
5) Acceptance gating: we propose p95 <= 180ms for short streaming at 100% expected load and p95 <= 260ms for long flows.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1: deliver microbenchmark report + recommended GPU type and pool size ranges.
- Week 2: run synthetic load and concurrency sweep; produce runbook notes and a gating recommendation.
- Week 3: optional joint validation with Novus traffic (via shared CSV or recorded traces).

Attachments: I attached a draft SLO matrix (novus_slo_matrix.xlsx) and our quick benchmark comparison (h100_vs_a100_benchmarks.pdf).

Next steps / asks:
- Caroline: confirm the 80/20 short/long split and whether we should include a multi-tenant stress test.
- Novus to share a sample traffic CSV or example prompt set (we discussed secure transfer via Drive).

If that all looks reasonable I’ll schedule a 30-min validation kickoff with Marcus and Ava to lock the test windows.

Thanks,

Nikhil — good notes. A couple of engineering clarifications before we run the baseline: 

1) Prompt mix detail: we need explicit token-per-request distribution. The 80/20 split is fine, but is that by request count or by tokens? That changes throughput shaping.
2) KV cache semantics: are sessions sticky to a user id or to a conversation id? If sticky to user id we can expect >60% cache hit for returning sessions which materially improves p95.
3) Burst characterization: when you say spikes to 8k tps, is that sustained for 1–2 minutes or 10–15 minutes? This affects queuing/backpressure behavior.

Proposed test matrix additions:
- Add a "cold start" then warm-up phase: 0–10 mins no-cache, then 30 mins steady to reach warm cache.
- Include a test where we inject 20% synthetic latency (network) to validate graceful degradation/fallback.

Operational notes:
- For Dedicated validation we’ll need a 4–6 hour window at low production load on the target infra; prefer US-PDT 10:00–16:00 slot.
- I’ll prepare a runner to capture per-token latency and KV hit rate; need Novus to map user/session IDs in sample CSV to ensure correct replay.

If Caroline confirms the token math and shares CSV we can start Week 1 microbenchmarks end of this week.

Marcus
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks Nikhil — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. Quick answers to Marcus: 

- Token split: 80/20 by request count (short requests are ~40–80 tokens; long are ~600–1,200 tokens). Our average tokens per second target is based on request count mix.
- Session stickiness: sticky by conversation id (users may have multiple conversations). Expect ~45% repeat prefixes within 24h.
- Burst duration: spikes typically last 3–7 minutes during peak usage. Occasionally longer during special events.

I uploaded a sample CSV called novus_sample_traffic.csv to the Drive folder you linked — it includes timestamp, conversation_id, prompt_type, and sample prompt text. Feel free to use that for the joint validation.

We’re happy to proceed with Week 1 microbenchmarks this week. Can you confirm an ETA for the microbenchmark report and the proposed GPU recommendation? Also, we’d prefer H100 if it reduces p95 materially, but we need a cost estimate for the Dedicated pool once you have the sizing.
